profile.campus: Silicon Valley (San Jose/Santa Clara), California (Equinix's founding market, Great Oaks/Corvin/Duane campuses)
profile.address: 5 Great Oaks Blvd, San Jose, CA 95119
profile.reading:
This building is Equinix's SV11 facility, part of Equinix's Silicon Valley data center network in the San Jose/Santa Clara area. Equinix was founded in 1998 by Al Avery and Jay Adelson, both former Digital Equipment Corporation facilities managers, on the idea of building a neutral place where competing internet networks could physically connect and exchange traffic, a model that let the company grow through network effects as more networks joined; Equinix converted to a real estate investment trust in January 2015 and trades on Nasdaq as EQIX. Silicon Valley, where Equinix is still headquartered today in nearby Redwood City, was the company's founding market, and its San Jose facilities on Great Oaks Boulevard and its Santa Clara facilities on Corvin Drive and Duane Avenue grew into one of the densest interconnection hubs in Equinix's global network as the company expanded internationally, entering Asia-Pacific in 2002, Europe via the IXEurope acquisition in 2007, Latin America in 2011, and the Middle East in 2013, and opening its 50th global data center in London by 2010 around the time it acquired Switch and Data Facilities Company. Equinix's own published specifications for the flagship SV1 building on this campus describe an 82,850-square-foot, single-story, steel-frame facility with N+1 power redundancy, a minimum cabinet density of 2kVA, 120v/208v power distribution, and generators rated for 30 hours or more at full load; Equinix markets the Great Oaks campus for its direct connections to major networks and tier-1 cloud service providers. Equinix's website did not disclose this specific building's own square footage or power capacity separately from the SV1 figure cited as representative of the broader campus.

Pacific Gas and Electric, the regional utility serving most of Silicon Valley, and Silicon Valley Power, Santa Clara's municipal utility, have both cited sustained data center load growth across the San Jose-Santa Clara-Sunnyvale corridor in their own capacity planning, a dynamic distinct from the newer data center markets elsewhere in the country given how built-out and power-constrained the Bay Area grid already is after decades of continuous data center development since Equinix's own 1998 founding in the area.

reading.body:
Equinix SV11 is a 121,930 square foot retail colocation facility in San Jose with N+1 power and N+2 cooling redundancy, rated for a minimum cabinet density of 5 kilowatts per cabinet. No megawatt power capacity is published for this building, so its actual load serving capability cannot be determined from operator specifications.

The facility is one of 12 buildings in Equinix's Silicon Valley metro footprint, which Equinix describes as the region's largest retail colocation campus. California has 103 mapped data center facilities overall, but only 11 publish power capacity figures totaling 365 megawatts. SV11 does not contribute to this published total, meaning its power specifications remain undisclosed while other facilities in the state have made theirs known.

Without disclosed power specifications, SV11's role in AI scaling cannot be assessed from available data. The facility serves a large customer base of enterprises and network service providers in a dense metro area, but whether it supplies power and cooling at the densities required for GPU clusters, storage systems, or AI training workloads depends on technical commitments Equinix has not made public.
